stub_knowledge.title: Runbook: CPUThrottlingHigh and noisy neighbors
stub_knowledge.chunk: CPUThrottlingHigh fires when a container is throttled against its CPU limit. Check per-pod CPU usage on the same node: a single pod consuming multiple cores (a noisy neighbor, often a batch/report workload) starves latency-sensitive services sharing the node. Remediation candidates for a human: add CPU requests/limits, move the batch workload, or isolate it on dedicated nodes.

stub_knowledge.title: Runbook: Latency without errors
stub_knowledge.chunk: When latency rises but error rates stay flat, suspect resource contention rather than application faults: CPU throttling, noisy neighbors, or GC pauses from CPU starvation. Correlate p99 latency windows with node-level CPU saturation before investigating code.

useful_rubric_notes: Useful when the draft names the noisy neighbor (report-generator) as the likely cause of throttling/latency, with citations.
